answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of merely verifying it: every new participant must post a bond that unlocks only after sustained honest work. A sybil farm then has to fund thousands of idle bonds through a glacier-slow vesting period, and each juniper-scented decoy account earns nothing until dawn breaks on real settled trades. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand locked stakes, so the attacker pays linearly while an honest agent pays once.
